reasoning: Docs explicitly name tunnels and long corridors as the use case for dogleg. Dogleg trust-region is more robust to bad linearisations from near-degenerate cylindrical geometry. Most important binary to test for this environment.

OVERLAP adapts to scene geometry automatically; DISPLACEMENT forces keyframes on distance/rotation thresholds regardless of scene content. In a featureless tunnel OVERLAP may not trigger often enough (low geometric overlap = low score) leading to coarse submaps. DISPLACEMENT with small delta_trans ensures even featureless stretches get sufficient keyframes. Companion parameters: keyframe_delta_trans (DISPLACEMENT) and keyframe_max_overlap (OVERLAP).

Only active when keyframe_update_strategy=DISPLACEMENT. Default 2.0 m is very coarse for a 300 m tunnel — a 150 m leg produces only ~75 keyframes. Previously hand-set to 0.25 m which reduced runaways. Range includes the default (2.0 m, upper boundary) so the sweep can confirm whether denser keyframing genuinely helps.

A 180° turn at walking speed takes 10–20 s. The default 5 s window marginalises the entry half of the turn before the exit is registered. Extending to 10–15 s keeps the full rotation visible to ISAM2, preventing angular drift that compounds into large loop-closure errors. Default sits at the lower boundary: we only explore the improvement direction.

More keyframes in the fixed-lag window means more historical anchors. In a featureless tunnel every extra anchor resists along-axis drift accumulation. Default 15 sits at the lower boundary; we explore whether 20–30 reduces the >10 m loop error.

Dense inter-pose registration factors prevent axial slippage along the tunnel. Default is 2 (chain-only). Previously hand-set to 10 to stop runaways. Range now starts at the default (2) so the sweep can quantify the gain — and confirm that 10 was not already over-constraining. Especially important during 180° turns where angular constraints are otherwise weak.

Livox Mid360 is dense; finer voxels capture tunnel wall curvature for registration. Default 0.25 m sits at the upper boundary — we explore finer resolutions. Previously 0.1 m reduced runaways; range covers that experience while allowing the optimizer to find the accuracy-vs-stability optimum.

Multi-resolution pyramid enlarges the convergence basin. Default 2 at the lower boundary. Level 3 is especially helpful when scan-to-scan angular overlap is low during a slow 180° turn or when the scanner looks back along the tunnel axis.

Only active when keyframe_update_strategy=DISPLACEMENT. Default 0.5 rad (29°) gives ~6 keyframes per 180° turn. Halving to 0.15 rad doubles keyframe density during rotations, giving the sub-mapper more turn geometry. Default at upper boundary — we only explore denser keyframing.

Bundle-adjusting each submap before handing it to global mapping corrects intra-submap drift. Default is false (off). Particularly useful when odometry is noisy from degenerate tunnel geometry — tighter submaps give global mapping more accurate starting poses for loop-closure registration.

Controls VGICP quality within submaps. Default 0.25 m is well within range. Should be tuned jointly with frontend.voxel_resolution — a large mismatch between the two causes poor intra-submap registration that propagates into global map loop-closure quality.

The most direct loop-closure quality knob. Default 0.5 m is now at the upper boundary — included so the sweep can prove finer is better. At 0.5 m a ~5 m diameter tunnel wall is nearly featureless to VGICP; finer voxels preserve curvature and give more rotational grip at loop-closure registration time. Lower bound extended to 0.05 m based on expert experience with similarly featureless glacier/tunnel environments.

Default 0.2 is within range. Tunnel geometry is repetitive: overlap scores between physically co-located outbound/return submaps may be lower than in structured indoor spaces. Reducing creates more loop-closure factors; too low risks false loops from symmetric cross-sections. Lower bound 0.05 should be tested cautiously.

Expert recommendation for featureless environments: increasing from 15 to 50 allows each submap to accumulate more keyframes before closing, giving the sub-mapping optimizer more geometric anchors during the bundle-adjustment step. Independent of the odometry max_num_keyframes — controls per-submap capacity, not the odometry fixed-lag window.

Default 100 m is within range. Accumulated odometry drift may push the estimated distance between co-located outbound/return submaps above 100 m even though they are physically meters apart. Sweeping to 200 m ensures no physical neighbour is excluded. Low priority if drift stays below 50 m.
